title: Atlas of Protein Sequence and Structure
authors: Dayhoff MO, Eck RV, Chang MA, Sochard MR
summary: The first comprehensive compilation of protein sequences, effectively the first bioinformatics database and the template for later sequence databanks.

title: A model of evolutionary change in proteins
authors: Dayhoff MO, Schwartz RM, Orcutt BC
venue: Atlas of Protein Sequence and Structure 5(Suppl 3):345-352
summary: Introduced the PAM (point accepted mutation) substitution matrices derived from closely related sequences, the standard scoring scheme for protein alignment for decades.

title: A general method applicable to the search for similarities in the amino acid sequence of two proteins
authors: Needleman SB, Wunsch CD
summary: Introduced dynamic programming for optimal global alignment of two sequences, the algorithmic foundation of sequence comparison.

title: Identification of common molecular subsequences
authors: Smith TF, Waterman MS
summary: Adapted dynamic programming to find optimal local alignments, the rigorous basis for detecting shared domains and for database search.

title: Evolutionary trees from DNA sequences: a maximum likelihood approach
authors: Felsenstein J
summary: Introduced practical maximum-likelihood phylogenetic inference with the pruning algorithm, the statistical foundation of modern molecular phylogenetics.

title: The GenBank genetic sequence databank
authors: Bilofsky HS, Burks C, Fickett JW, Goad WB, Lewitter FI, Rindone WP, et al.
summary: Described GenBank, the public nucleotide sequence archive established in 1982 at Los Alamos and later run by NCBI, a core shared resource of genomics.

title: Improved tools for biological sequence comparison
authors: Pearson WR, Lipman DJ
summary: Introduced the FASTA program, a fast k-tuple heuristic for sensitive database similarity search that preceded BLAST.

title: Basic local alignment search tool
authors: Altschul SF, Gish W, Miller W, Myers EW, Lipman DJ
summary: Introduced BLAST, a fast seed-and-extend heuristic with rigorous statistics for local alignment search, becoming one of the most-used tools in biology.

title: Amino acid substitution matrices from protein blocks
authors: Henikoff S, Henikoff JG
summary: Derived the BLOSUM substitution matrices from conserved blocks of distant homologs; BLOSUM62 became the default protein scoring matrix.

title: CLUSTAL W: improving the sensitivity of progressive multiple sequence alignment through sequence weighting, position-specific gap penalties and weight matrix choice
authors: Thompson JD, Higgins DG, Gibson TJ
summary: The widely used progressive multiple sequence alignment program, making MSAs routine for evolutionary and structural analysis.

title: Hidden Markov models in computational biology: applications to protein modeling
authors: Krogh A, Brown M, Mian IS, Sjölander K, Haussler D
summary: Introduced profile hidden Markov models for protein families, giving a probabilistic framework for homology detection and alignment.

title: Pfam: a comprehensive database of protein domain families based on seed alignments
authors: Sonnhammer EL, Eddy SR, Durbin R
summary: Created Pfam, the curated database of protein domain families represented as profile HMMs, a standard resource for annotation and later for MSA-based structure prediction.

title: Gapped BLAST and PSI-BLAST: a new generation of protein database search programs
authors: Altschul SF, Madden TL, Schäffer AA, Zhang J, Zhang Z, Miller W, et al.
summary: Added gapped alignment and iterative position-specific scoring (PSI-BLAST) to BLAST, greatly improving remote homology detection and supplying profiles to structure predictors.

title: Profile hidden Markov models
authors: Eddy SR
summary: Reviewed and popularized profile HMMs and the HMMER software for sensitive protein family search.

title: An Eulerian path approach to DNA fragment assembly
authors: Pevzner PA, Tang H, Waterman MS
summary: Recast genome assembly as finding Eulerian paths in a de Bruijn graph, the paradigm adopted by short-read assemblers.

title: Velvet: algorithms for de novo short read assembly using de Bruijn graphs
authors: Zerbino DR, Birney E
summary: A practical de Bruijn graph assembler for next-generation short reads, enabling de novo assembly of genomes from Illumina data.

title: Fast and accurate short read alignment with Burrows-Wheeler transform
authors: Li H, Durbin R
summary: Introduced BWA, using the Burrows-Wheeler transform and FM-index to map short reads quickly to large genomes; a backbone of resequencing pipelines.

title: Ultrafast and memory-efficient alignment of short DNA sequences to the human genome
authors: Langmead B, Trapnell C, Pop M, Salzberg SL
summary: Introduced Bowtie, a Burrows-Wheeler-indexed short-read aligner that made mapping to the human genome fast on ordinary hardware.

title: The Genome Analysis Toolkit: a MapReduce framework for analyzing next-generation DNA sequencing data
authors: McKenna A, Hanna M, Banks E, Sivachenko A, Cibulskis K, Kernytsky A, et al.
summary: Introduced GATK, the standard framework for variant discovery and genotyping from high-throughput sequencing.

title: Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2
authors: Love MI, Huber W, Anders S
summary: Introduced DESeq2, a negative-binomial shrinkage method for differential expression analysis that became a standard for RNA-seq.

title: Spatial reconstruction of single-cell gene expression data
authors: Satija R, Farrell JA, Gennert D, Schier AF, Regev A
summary: Introduced Seurat, which grew into the dominant R toolkit for single-cell RNA-seq clustering, integration and analysis.

title: MMseqs2 enables sensitive protein sequence searching for the analysis of massive data sets
authors: Steinegger M, Söding J
summary: A very fast sensitive protein search tool that made searches against billions of sequences practical; later powered ColabFold MSA generation.

title: SCANPY: large-scale single-cell gene expression data analysis
authors: Wolf FA, Angerer P, Theis FJ
summary: A scalable Python framework for single-cell analysis that anchors the scverse ecosystem.

title: The reflection of X-rays by crystals
authors: Bragg WH, Bragg WL
summary: Established Bragg's law and X-ray crystal structure analysis, the origin of crystallography as a tool for atomic structure.

title: The structure of proteins: two hydrogen-bonded helical configurations of the polypeptide chain
authors: Pauling L, Corey RB, Branson HR
summary: Predicted the alpha-helix from stereochemical principles, founding the idea of regular protein secondary structure.

title: A three-dimensional model of the myoglobin molecule obtained by X-ray analysis
authors: Kendrew JC, Bodo G, Dintzis HM, Parrish RG, Wyckoff H, Phillips DC
summary: The first three-dimensional structure of a protein (myoglobin), proving that protein structures could be solved by X-ray crystallography.

title: Structure of haemoglobin: a three-dimensional Fourier synthesis at 5.5-Å resolution, obtained by X-ray analysis
authors: Perutz MF, Rossmann MG, Cullis AF, Muirhead H, Will G, North ACT
summary: Solved haemoglobin using heavy-atom isomorphous replacement, opening the way to structure-function understanding of allostery; Nobel Prize 1962 with Kendrew.

title: Stereochemistry of polypeptide chain configurations
authors: Ramachandran GN, Ramakrishnan C, Sasisekharan V
summary: Introduced the Ramachandran plot of allowed backbone phi/psi angles, still the basic validation of protein structures and a constraint for prediction.

title: The Protein Data Bank: a computer-based archival file for macromolecular structures
authors: Bernstein FC, Koetzle TF, Williams GJ, Meyer EF Jr, Brice MD, Rodgers JR, et al.
summary: Described the Protein Data Bank archive founded in 1971, the shared repository of macromolecular coordinates.

title: Solution conformation of proteinase inhibitor IIA from bull seminal plasma by 1H nuclear magnetic resonance and distance geometry
authors: Williamson MP, Havel TF, Wüthrich K
summary: The first complete protein structure determined by NMR in solution, establishing NMR as a second route to atomic protein structures (Wüthrich, Nobel 2002).

title: Cryo-electron microscopy of vitrified specimens
authors: Dubochet J, Adrian M, Chang JJ, Homo JC, Lepault J, McDowall AW, et al.
summary: Established vitrification of thin aqueous specimens in amorphous ice, the sample preparation underlying all biological cryo-EM (Nobel 2017).

title: Model for the structure of bacteriorhodopsin based on high-resolution electron cryo-microscopy
authors: Henderson R, Baldwin JM, Ceska TA, Zemlin F, Beckmann E, Downing KH
summary: The first atomic model of a membrane protein from electron cryo-microscopy, showing EM could reach near-atomic resolution (Nobel 2017).

title: Three-Dimensional Electron Microscopy of Macromolecular Assemblies
authors: Frank J
summary: Codified single-particle reconstruction, the image-processing framework (alignment, classification, 3D reconstruction) developed by Frank and used by all single-particle cryo-EM (Nobel 2017).

title: The Protein Data Bank
authors: Berman HM, Westbrook J, Feng Z, Gilliland G, Bhat TN, Weissig H, et al.
summary: Described the modernized RCSB Protein Data Bank, the curated archive of experimental structures whose ~200,000 entries trained AlphaFold and successors.

title: RELION: implementation of a Bayesian approach to cryo-EM structure determination
authors: Scheres SHW
summary: Introduced Bayesian (maximum a posteriori) refinement for single-particle cryo-EM, central to the resolution revolution.

title: Electron counting and beam-induced motion correction enable near-atomic-resolution single-particle cryo-EM
authors: Li X, Mooney P, Zheng S, Booth CR, Braunfeld MB, Gubbens S, et al.
summary: Showed that direct electron detectors with motion correction enable near-atomic resolution, a key enabler of the cryo-EM resolution revolution.

title: Structure of the TRPV1 ion channel determined by electron cryo-microscopy
authors: Liao M, Cao E, Julius D, Cheng Y
summary: A 3.4 Å single-particle cryo-EM structure of a membrane protein without crystals, the emblematic result of the resolution revolution.

title: The resolution revolution
authors: Kühlbrandt W
summary: Named and documented the 2013-2014 jump of cryo-EM to near-atomic resolution driven by direct detectors and new software.

title: cryoSPARC: algorithms for rapid unsupervised cryo-EM structure determination
authors: Punjani A, Rubinstein JL, Fleet DJ, Brubaker MA
summary: Introduced stochastic gradient descent ab initio reconstruction and branch-and-bound refinement, making cryo-EM processing fast and accessible.

title: Single-particle cryo-EM at atomic resolution
authors: Nakane T, Kotecha A, Sente A, McMullan G, Masiulis S, Brown PMGE, et al.
summary: Reached ~1.2 Å resolution for apoferritin, resolving individual atoms and hydrogens and establishing cryo-EM as a true atomic-resolution method.

title: How to fold graciously
authors: Levinthal C
venue: Mössbauer Spectroscopy in Biological Systems, Univ. Illinois Press, pp. 22-24
summary: Posed Levinthal's paradox: random conformational search would take astronomically long, so folding must follow guided pathways.

title: Principles that govern the folding of protein chains
authors: Anfinsen CB
summary: Nobel lecture stating the thermodynamic hypothesis: the amino acid sequence determines the native structure, the premise of structure prediction.

title: Spin glasses and the statistical mechanics of protein folding
authors: Bryngelson JD, Wolynes PG
summary: Introduced energy-landscape theory and the principle of minimal frustration, resolving Levinthal's paradox via funneled landscapes.

title: A new approach to protein fold recognition
authors: Jones DT, Taylor WR, Thornton JM
summary: Introduced threading, scoring sequence fit to known folds with pairwise potentials, to recognize folds beyond detectable homology.

title: Prediction of protein secondary structure at better than 70% accuracy
authors: Rost B, Sander C
summary: PHD combined neural networks with multiple sequence alignment profiles, a decisive early use of evolutionary information and machine learning for prediction.

title: Comparative protein modelling by satisfaction of spatial restraints
authors: Šali A, Blundell TL
summary: Introduced MODELLER, the standard homology-modeling approach that builds models from template-derived spatial restraints.

title: A large-scale experiment to assess protein structure prediction methods
authors: Moult J, Pedersen JT, Judson R, Fidelis K
summary: Launched CASP, the blind biennial assessment of structure prediction that defined progress in the field and later certified AlphaFold.

title: Assembly of protein tertiary structures from fragments with similar local sequences using simulated annealing and Bayesian scoring functions
authors: Simons KT, Kooperberg C, Huang E, Baker D
summary: Introduced Rosetta fragment-assembly de novo structure prediction, the basis of the Rosetta suite for both prediction and design.

title: Protein 3D structure computed from evolutionary sequence variation
authors: Marks DS, Colwell LJ, Sheridan R, Hopf TA, Pagnani A, Zecchina R, et al.
summary: EVfold used global maximum-entropy models of coevolution to infer residue contacts and fold proteins de novo from sequence families alone.

title: Accurate de novo prediction of protein contact map by ultra-deep learning model
authors: Wang S, Sun S, Li Z, Zhang R, Xu J
summary: RaptorX-Contact applied deep residual networks to coevolution features, dramatically improving contact prediction in CASP12.

title: Improved protein structure prediction using potentials from deep learning
authors: Senior AW, Evans R, Jumper J, Kirkpatrick J, Sifre L, Green T, et al.
summary: AlphaFold (CASP13) predicted inter-residue distance distributions with deep networks and folded proteins by gradient descent on the resulting potential.

title: Improved protein structure prediction using predicted interresidue orientations
authors: Yang J, Anishchenko I, Park H, Peng Z, Ovchinnikov S, Baker D
summary: trRosetta predicted inter-residue distances and orientations to drive Rosetta folding, a fast open alternative to AlphaFold 1.

title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
authors: Jumper J, Evans R, Pritzel A, Green T, Figurnov M, Ronneberger O, et al.
summary: AlphaFold2's Evoformer and structure module reached near-experimental accuracy in CASP14, largely solving single-chain protein structure prediction (Nobel 2024).

title: Accurate prediction of protein structures and interactions using a three-track neural network
authors: Baek M, DiMaio F, Anishchenko I, Dauparas J, Ovchinnikov S, Lee GR, et al.
summary: RoseTTAFold jointly reasoned over sequence, distance and 3D coordinates, achieving near-AlphaFold2 accuracy openly and modeling complexes.

title: Protein complex prediction with AlphaFold-Multimer
authors: Evans R, O'Neill M, Pritzel A, Antropova N, Senior A, Green T, et al.
summary: Retrained AlphaFold for multi-chain inputs, substantially improving prediction of protein-protein complexes.

title: AlphaFold Protein Structure Database: massively expanding the structural coverage of protein-sequence space with high-accuracy models
authors: Varadi M, Anyango S, Deshpande M, Nair S, Natassia C, Yordanova G, et al.
summary: The AlphaFold DB with EMBL-EBI, later expanded to over 200 million predicted structures covering nearly all of UniProt.

title: Evolutionary-scale prediction of atomic-level protein structure with a language model
authors: Lin Z, Akin H, Rao R, Hie B, Zhu Z, Lu W, et al.
summary: ESM-2 and ESMFold predicted structures from single sequences with a protein language model, enabling the ~600-million-structure ESM Metagenomic Atlas.

title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
authors: Abramson J, Adler J, Dunger J, Evans R, Green T, Pritzel A, et al.
summary: AlphaFold 3 replaced the structure module with a diffusion model to predict joint structures of proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, ions and modifications.

title: Generalized biomolecular modeling and design with RoseTTAFold All-Atom
authors: Krishna R, Wang J, Ahern W, Sturmfels P, Venkatesh P, Kalvet I, et al.
summary: Extended RoseTTAFold to all-atom modeling of proteins with small molecules, metals, nucleic acids and covalent modifications, and enabled RFdiffusion All-Atom design.

title: Boltz-1: Democratizing biomolecular interaction modeling
authors: Wohlwend J, Corso G, Passaro S, Reveiz M, Leidal K, Swiderski W, et al.
summary: The first fully open-source model reaching AlphaFold 3-level accuracy on biomolecular complexes, with code and weights under a permissive license.

title: Filamentous fusion phage: novel expression vectors that display cloned antigens on the virion surface
authors: Smith GP
summary: Invented phage display, linking genotype to displayed protein for library selection of binders and antibodies (Nobel 2018).

title: Tuning the activity of an enzyme for unusual environments: sequential random mutagenesis of subtilisin E for catalysis in dimethylformamide
authors: Chen K, Arnold FH
summary: Demonstrated directed evolution of enzymes by iterative random mutagenesis and screening (Arnold, Nobel 2018).

title: De novo protein design: fully automated sequence selection
authors: Dahiyat BI, Mayo SL
summary: The first fully computationally designed sequence for a protein fold (a zinc-finger fold), validating physics-based automated design.

title: Design of a novel globular protein fold with atomic-level accuracy
authors: Kuhlman B, Dantas G, Ireton GC, Varani G, Stoddard BL, Baker D
summary: Designed Top7, a protein with a fold not seen in nature, whose crystal structure matched the Rosetta model with atomic accuracy.

title: Kemp elimination catalysts by computational enzyme design
authors: Röthlisberger D, Khersonsky O, Wollacott AM, Jiang L, DeChancie J, Betker J, et al.
summary: Computationally designed enzymes for a reaction with no natural catalyst, later improved by directed evolution.

title: De novo computational design of retro-aldol enzymes
authors: Jiang L, Althoff EA, Clemente FR, Doyle L, Röthlisberger D, Zanghellini A, et al.
summary: Designed active retro-aldolases with multistep mechanisms using Rosetta theozyme placement, a landmark in de novo enzyme design.

title: Proof of principle for epitope-focused vaccine design
authors: Correia BE, Bates JT, Loomis RJ, Baneyx G, Carrico C, Jardine JG, et al.
summary: Computationally designed scaffolds presenting an RSV neutralizing epitope that elicited neutralizing antibodies in macaques.

title: Elicitation of potent neutralizing antibody responses by designed protein nanoparticle vaccines for SARS-CoV-2
authors: Walls AC, Fiala B, Schäfer A, Wrenn S, Pham MN, Murphy M, et al.
summary: A computationally designed two-component nanoparticle displaying the spike RBD; it became SKYCovione, the first approved vaccine built on a de novo designed protein.

title: Design of protein-binding proteins from the target structure alone
authors: Cao L, Coventry B, Goreshnik I, Huang B, Sheffler W, Park JS, et al.
summary: A general Rosetta pipeline producing de novo binders to diverse targets using only the target structure.

title: Robust deep learning-based protein sequence design using ProteinMPNN
authors: Dauparas J, Anishchenko I, Bennett N, Bai H, Ragotte RJ, Milles LF, et al.
summary: A message-passing network for inverse folding that designs sequences for backbones with far higher experimental success than Rosetta.

title: Large language models generate functional protein sequences across diverse families
authors: Madani A, Krause B, Greene ER, Subramanian S, Mohr BP, Holton JM, et al.
summary: ProGen, a conditional protein language model, generated artificial lysozymes with natural-like activity despite low sequence identity.

title: De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion
authors: Watson JL, Juergens D, Bennett NR, Trippe BL, Yim J, Eisenach HE, et al.
summary: Fine-tuned RoseTTAFold as a denoising diffusion model over backbones, enabling design of binders, symmetric assemblies and motif scaffolds with high success.

title: Illuminating protein space with a programmable generative model
authors: Ingraham JB, Baranov M, Costello Z, Barber KW, Wang W, Ismail A, et al.
summary: Chroma, a diffusion model over protein complexes with programmable conditioning on symmetry, shape and semantics.

title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024: computational protein design and protein structure prediction
authors: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (laureates Baker D, Hassabis D, Jumper J)
summary: Awarded half to David Baker for computational protein design and half to Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for AlphaFold protein structure prediction.

title: Rapid in silico directed evolution by a protein language model with EVOLVEpro
authors: Jiang K, Yan Z, Di Bernardo M, Sgrizzi SR, Villiger L, Kayabolen A, et al.
summary: Combined protein language model embeddings with few-shot active learning to evolve antibodies, CRISPR nucleases and other proteins in few rounds.

title: Simulating 500 million years of evolution with a language model
authors: Hayes T, Rao R, Akin H, Sofroniew NJ, Oktay D, Lin Z, et al.
summary: ESM3, a multimodal generative model over sequence, structure and function tokens, generated a functional fluorescent protein (esmGFP) distant from known GFPs.

title: Die Kinetik der Invertinwirkung
authors: Michaelis L, Menten ML
summary: Derived the Michaelis-Menten rate law for enzyme kinetics, the foundational quantitative model of biochemistry.

title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
authors: Hodgkin AL, Huxley AF
summary: Coupled differential equations reproducing the action potential from measured ionic conductances, the archetype of mechanistic biological modeling (Nobel 1963).

title: The chemical basis of morphogenesis
authors: Turing AM
venue: Phil Trans R Soc Lond B 237(641):37-72
summary: Showed reaction-diffusion systems can spontaneously form patterns, founding mathematical theories of developmental pattern formation.

title: Metabolic stability and epigenesis in randomly constructed genetic nets
authors: Kauffman SA
summary: Introduced random Boolean networks as models of gene regulation, linking attractors to cell types.

title: Dynamics of folded proteins
authors: McCammon JA, Gelin BR, Karplus M
summary: The first molecular dynamics simulation of a protein (BPTI), revealing internal fluid-like motions.

title: Stoichiometric flux balance models quantitatively predict growth and metabolic by-product secretion in wild-type Escherichia coli W3110
authors: Varma A, Palsson BO
summary: Showed constraint-based flux balance analysis predicts E. coli growth and secretion quantitatively, launching genome-scale metabolic modeling.

title: The large-scale organization of metabolic networks
authors: Jeong H, Tombor B, Albert R, Oltvai ZN, Barabási AL
summary: Found scale-free topology across metabolic networks of 43 organisms, catalyzing network biology.

title: Systems biology: a brief overview
authors: Kitano H
summary: Influential manifesto defining systems biology as system-level understanding through structure, dynamics, control and design.

title: The systems biology markup language (SBML): a medium for representation and exchange of biochemical network models
authors: Hucka M, Finney A, Sauro HM, Bolouri H, Doyle JC, Kitano H, et al.
summary: Defined SBML, the standard exchange format for biochemical network models.

title: An Introduction to Systems Biology: Design Principles of Biological Circuits
authors: Alon U
summary: Textbook framing gene circuits through network motifs, robustness and optimal design.

title: Anton, a special-purpose machine for molecular dynamics simulation
authors: Shaw DE, Deneroff MM, Dror RO, Kuskin JS, Larson RH, Salmon JK, et al.
summary: A purpose-built supercomputer accelerating biomolecular MD by orders of magnitude, opening millisecond timescales.

title: Atomic-level characterization of the structural dynamics of proteins
authors: Shaw DE, Maragakis P, Lindorff-Larsen K, Piana S, Dror RO, Eastwood MP, et al.
summary: Millisecond-scale all-atom MD on Anton captured folding and native-state dynamics of small proteins.

title: A whole-cell computational model predicts phenotype from genotype
authors: Karr JR, Sanghvi JC, Macklin DN, Gutschow MV, Jacobs JM, Bolival B Jr, et al.
summary: The first whole-cell model, integrating 28 submodels to simulate the full life cycle of Mycoplasma genitalium.

title: p-σ-π Analysis. A method for the correlation of biological activity and chemical structure
authors: Hansch C, Fujita T
summary: Founded QSAR by regressing biological activity on hydrophobic, electronic and steric descriptors, the start of computational drug design.

title: A geometric approach to macromolecule-ligand interactions
authors: Kuntz ID, Blaney JM, Oatley SJ, Langridge R, Ferrin TE
summary: Introduced DOCK, the first molecular docking program, matching ligand shapes to receptor sites for structure-based drug design.

title: Automated docking using a Lamarckian genetic algorithm and an empirical binding free energy function
authors: Morris GM, Goodsell DS, Halliday RS, Huey R, Hart WE, Belew RK, et al.
summary: AutoDock 3 introduced a Lamarckian genetic algorithm and empirical free-energy scoring, becoming a widely used docking tool.

title: AutoDock Vina: improving the speed and accuracy of docking with a new scoring function, efficient optimization, and multithreading
authors: Trott O, Olson AJ
summary: A fast, accurate open-source docking program that became the most widely used docking engine.

title: Predicting the sequence specificities of DNA- and RNA-binding proteins by deep learning
authors: Alipanahi B, Delong A, Weirauch MT, Frey BJ
summary: DeepBind applied convolutional networks to learn protein-nucleic acid binding specificities, an early landmark of deep learning in genomics.

title: Predicting effects of noncoding variants with deep learning-based sequence model
authors: Zhou J, Troyanskaya OG
summary: DeepSEA predicted chromatin features from sequence and scored effects of noncoding variants.

title: Automatic chemical design using a data-driven continuous representation of molecules
authors: Gómez-Bombarelli R, Wei JN, Duvenaud D, Hernández-Lobato JM, Sánchez-Lengeling B, Sheberla D, et al.
summary: Used a variational autoencoder to map molecules to a continuous latent space for gradient-based generative molecular design.

title: Deep generative models of genetic variation capture the effects of mutations
authors: Riesselman AJ, Ingraham JB, Marks DS
summary: DeepSequence used VAEs on protein family alignments to predict mutation effects without labels.

title: Ultra-large library docking for discovering new chemotypes
authors: Lyu J, Wang S, Balius TE, Singh I, Levit A, Moroz YS, et al.
summary: Docked ~170 million make-on-demand molecules, finding potent novel ligands and showing hit rates improve with library scale.

title: Deep learning enables rapid identification of potent DDR1 kinase inhibitors
authors: Zhavoronkov A, Ivanenkov YA, Aliper A, Veselov MS, Aladinskiy VA, Aladinskaya AV, et al.
summary: GENTRL, a generative reinforcement-learning model, designed DDR1 inhibitors validated in cells and mice within weeks.

title: A deep learning approach to antibiotic discovery
authors: Stokes JM, Yang K, Swanson K, Jin W, Cubillos-Ruiz A, Donghia NM, et al.
summary: A graph neural network screen identified halicin, a structurally novel broad-spectrum antibiotic, showcasing deep learning for drug discovery.

title: Biological structure and function emerge from scaling unsupervised learning to 250 million protein sequences
authors: Rives A, Meier J, Sercu T, Goyal S, Lin Z, Liu J, et al.
summary: ESM-1b trained a Transformer masked language model on UniRef protein sequences; its representations encoded structure, contacts and function without supervision.

title: Effective gene expression prediction from sequence by integrating long-range interactions
authors: Avsec Ž, Agarwal V, Visentin D, Ledsam JR, Grabska-Barwinska A, Taylor KR, et al.
summary: Enformer used Transformer attention over ~200 kb of DNA to predict gene expression and chromatin, improving variant-effect prediction.

title: DiffDock: Diffusion steps, twists, and turns for molecular docking
authors: Corso G, Stärk H, Jing B, Barzilay R, Jaakkola T
summary: Framed docking as generative diffusion over ligand translations, rotations and torsions, outperforming search-based docking on blind benchmarks.

title: Transfer learning enables predictions in network biology
authors: Theodoris CV, Xiao L, Chopra A, Chaffin MD, Al Sayed ZR, Hill MC, et al.
summary: Geneformer pretrained a Transformer on ~30 million single-cell transcriptomes, enabling transfer learning for network biology tasks.

title: Accurate proteome-wide missense variant effect prediction with AlphaMissense
authors: Cheng J, Novati G, Pan J, Bycroft C, Žemgulytė A, Applebaum T, et al.
summary: Adapted AlphaFold with protein language modeling to classify 71 million possible human missense variants as likely benign or pathogenic.

title: scGPT: toward building a foundation model for single-cell multi-omics using generative AI
authors: Cui H, Wang C, Maan H, Pang K, Luo F, Duan N, et al.
summary: A generative Transformer pretrained on over 33 million cells for cell-type annotation, integration and perturbation prediction.

title: Discovery of a structural class of antibiotics with explainable deep learning
authors: Wong F, Zheng EJ, Valeri JA, Donghia NM, Anahtar MN, Omori S, et al.
summary: Explainable graph neural network substructure search discovered a new structural class of antibiotics active against MRSA.

title: A small-molecule TNIK inhibitor targets fibrosis in preclinical and clinical models
authors: Ren F, Aliper A, Chen J, Zhao H, Rao S, Kuppe C, et al.
summary: Described INS018_055 (rentosertib), an AI-nominated target and AI-generated TNIK inhibitor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis that advanced to positive phase 2a trials.

title: Sequence modeling and design from molecular to genome scale with Evo
authors: Nguyen E, Poli M, Durrant MG, Kang B, Katrekar D, Li DB, et al.
summary: Evo, a 7B-parameter long-context DNA language model trained on prokaryotic genomes, predicted fitness and generated functional CRISPR-Cas and transposon systems.

title: Genome modeling and design across all domains of life with Evo 2
authors: Brixi G, Durrant MG, Ku J, Poli M, Brockman G, Chang D, et al.
summary: Evo 2 scaled DNA language modeling to 40B parameters and 1-Mb context on genomes across the tree of life, enabling zero-shot variant-effect prediction including BRCA1.
